My experience with Sarah Speed and Herrington Carmichael was catastrophic both emotionally and financially.

This was not a billionaire divorce involving companies, offshore trusts or vast assets. I owned one ordinary 3-bedroom house and there were no children involved, yet I was still billed close to £180,000 in legal fees over the course of proceedings.

When I eventually questioned the scale of the billing and refused to blindly accept it, the reaction was immediate and aggressive. Barristers were instructed against me and pressure intensified instead of any meaningful attempt to justify or reflect on the costs being charged. She attempted to bill me £42,000 for a half day preliminary hearing to examine her billing, which was described as "bonkers" by the judge.

Importantly, during subsequent costs proceedings, the court reduced parts of the claimed costs, billing and hourly rates. That speaks for itself.

One letter she attempted to bill me was for £6700 ex VAT for just 7hrs of alleged work which was slapped down by a costs judge

What I experienced was a relentless cycle of escalating fees, excessive charging for correspondence, a revolving door of trainees and junior staff, and a complete absence of proportionality or common sense. At times it genuinely felt like the priority was maximising invoices rather than resolving the case sensibly.

At one stage Sarah was screaming down the phone at me that she needs to be paid. She also sent inappropriate messages from her personal phone. Sarah is about earning fees and your best interests are secondary.

Family proceedings are stressful enough without feeling financially destroyed by your own solicitors. In my opinion, this firm lost sight of the client entirely.

I also became uncomfortable with aspects of the professional boundaries during the retainer. Some communications sent to me via WhatsApp from a personal phone felt overly informal and, in my view, inappropriate within a solicitor-client relationship.

The only decent lawyer was a trainee Toby Glass, who left the firm once he qualified. That speaks for itself.

If you are considering instructing this firm, question every invoice, scrutinise every hourly rate, and do not assume that eye-watering fees equate to quality representation.

Avoid this firm like the plague! They made mistake after mistake when dealing with my Dad's simple will. Their communication was terrible and their fees ended up being over double what they originally quoted us. It was a really terrible experience and I hope no one else has to endure this pain.
If I could submit 0 stars I would have.

I chose Chooi Leng after attending her workshop, where she appeared friendly and knowledgeable. However, this decision has ultimately proved to be a costly and time-consuming experience without a usable outcome. Based on our experience, I would not recommend her service.

Having recently moved to the UK, I relied on her to guide us through what was a completely new process. Our garden is around one acre, and we made it clear from the outset that our budget was approximately £20,000 (with limited flexibility) — this was precisely why we engaged a designer.

However, our experience raised several concerns:

* Budget misalignment: The design led to contractor quotes starting from £60,000, far exceeding our stated budget
* Inaccurate measurements: Patio dimensions in the design were later found to be incorrect when reviewed by the contractor
* Existing planting ignored: Mature camellias and hydrangeas around the house were effectively removed in the design, rather than incorporated
* Lack of accountability: Requests to revise the layout based on correct measurements and existing conditions were declined
* Questionable value: A revised planting scheme was offered only if we determined ourselves which plants to retain, and within the existing layout — leaving it unclear what the designer’s role was intended to be in this process

Having paid over £3,000 in design fees, we are now left re-measuring the garden and reassessing planting ourselves.

Overall, this was not a practical or buildable design, and did not provide the guidance we expected from a professional service.

Dishonest and Untrustworthy. They are willing to go back on a purchase agreement on a car for their own financial benefit at the customers expense, despite collecting the car and retaining it without payment for over a month after agreeing to buy it. They then refused to pay the full agreed amount. Stuart at Rockhill motors initially offered the full amount in cash on collection. We wanted a bank transfer, he agreed to transfer the full amount when he returned to his office - he didn’t. Leaving us with no money and no car …. In depth story to follow.

Our car broke down away from our home address. We discovered Rockhill motors while searching for recovery companies near gillingham. Rockhill Motors recovered the Audi A4 and dropped it at our home address while we decided what to do with it. Stuart from rock hill motors mentioned that he buys used cars and would be interested in it for the right price. I then called Stuart a few days later as we had decided to sell the car as oppose to repairing it. The oil pressure warning light had come on which is why it was recovered. Stuart was fully informed of this and the car was described accurately and honestly, he was fully aware of the cause of the breakdown and had recovered it himself. When I called Stuart up we agreed on a price and a time to collect the car.

Stuart then arrived with his recovery truck a few days later to collect his new purchase. He brought cash with him for the full amount agreed. I suggested that we would prefer a bank transfer. He agreed and said he would transfer the money as soon as he had returned to his office that day. We had a good chat about used cars etc and his plans for the Audi. Therefore, I trusted Stuart to transfer it once he returned to the office and didn’t feel the need to hold back the car until he has paid, particularly as his business is approximately 15 minutes away from me.

The payment didn’t arrive that night and I began to get suspicious. Stuart then calls me the day after and I question him as to why the money hasn’t arrived yet. He states “there is a problem”. Stuart had gone ahead and started investigating the cause of the low oil pressure further. He then told me that the turbo had failed and he was no longer interested in the car and he refused to pay despite the agreement and the fact he had taken the car away. The turbo failure is a part that fails as a direct result of low oil pressure which Stuart must know as a mechanic and he was given every opportunity to look over the car prior to making a purchase. Stuart then offered me less money than the agreed price, I did not accept as this was going against the agreement made and I had trusted him to make. I then contacted citizens advice etc, both of which informed me that Stuart must pay the full agreed amount. They also informed me that I had no obligation to accept the car back as it was not misdescribed. I did not want the car back either as Stuart had driven it with no oil pressure which results in further damage. He also worked on the vehicle without payment or permission to do so.

I am writing this after over a month in which Stuart has retained possession of the car and not paid for it. I have unfortunately due to financial reasons and the time and money involved with taking the matter further had to accept a lower amount from Rockhill motors. I do not recommend that you deal with Rockhill motors. Do not expect them to follow through with any deals that are made, do not expect to see all your money, expect to wait over a month to receive anything

Where do I even start. On the surface, Courier Exchange is a solid platform. There’s consistent workflow, and you can make decent money… if your only expense in life is fuel.

The problem is the downsides outweigh the positives, and most of them are completely avoidable and easily fixable.

For load posters, the platform is perfect. Jobs that should realistically be priced at £1–£1.50 per mile are regularly sold for around 60p per mile, while their end customer is being charged £2+ per mile. The margins are huge, which explains the constant flow of work. It works brilliantly for them, just not for the drivers actually doing the job.

Even with fuel costs where they are, rates haven’t adjusted. I understand companies don’t want to lose customers, but there still needs to be a baseline level of fairness.

Where CX falls short is failing to protect drivers. There’s nothing in place to ensure fair rates, so it turns into a bidding war, a race to the bottom. Bust fools. Drivers undercut each other just to win work, and many companies bidding on jobs are running hourly-paid drivers. That means they can afford to bid extremely low just to keep their driver moving, even if the job itself is barely profitable. It makes sense from a business perspective, but it destroys the market for everyone else.

This could be addressed with simple rules or safeguards around pricing. At the moment, there’s nothing.

Then there are payment terms. You secure a job at a decent rate, only to find 45 days end of month, or even 60-day terms. Meanwhile, fuel has already been paid for. And you have to wait 45-60 days for this money to come in…  Realistically, you need a cash float of around £5,000 just to stay operational while waiting to be paid, the money you’re entitled to, the money YOU worked for. It’s a joke.

So now what happens, drivers look for solutions like invoice factoring to maintain cash flow. BUT GUESS WHAT, CX has banned factoring altogether. Instead, they’ve introduced “SmartPay” and “Early Pay”, which only work if the load poster enables it, and 80%  don’t have it on😂

Okay let’s say it is available, the fees range from 15–25%. At that point, a large portion of your profit is gone instantly. It’s ridiculous.

This is another self-inflicted issue. CX could easily allow factoring again or introduce a fair, capped fee structure and make early payment standard across the platform without greedy fees. Instead, drivers are left with limited and expensive options.

I don’t even want to comment on the platform fees themselves, which by the way continue to increase year after year, with no justification. Lyall Cresswell is rubbing his hands together at the smell of the money.

Overall, the platform has potential and clearly works well for load posters, but drivers, who are the backbone of it, are left carrying most of the risk and cost.

Courier Exchange, please address these issues.

Joining them was the worse experience ever. Very unfair and definitely not accurate on the jobs they apply to be posting each day. Their prices rise again selectively up to members. Some get massive increase some none at all. If there was a zero i would gladly put a zero.

I rarely leave reviews but this needs to be said. Courier Exchange markets itself as a neutral and professional platform, but based on my experience that simply isn’t the case. A courier company, HBC Logistics, was allowed to operate while clearly breaching multiple Courier Exchange rules. They were posting jobs, collecting bids, then diverting drivers off-platform onto their own system (SmartLM), cancelling the jobs on CX, and continuing the work externally. Even more concerning, data linked to those jobs, including driver contact details, was then used to market directly to my drivers and encourage them to leave my company and join their platform. That is completely unacceptable and raises serious data protection concerns. Courier Exchange were provided with evidence of this behaviour yet allowed both HBC Logistics and the SmartLM integration to continue operating for a prolonged period. At the same time, SmartLM was presented as a partnered or trusted integration despite clearly being linked to a competing logistics company. When issues were raised, the responses were slow, generic and focused on deflecting responsibility rather than addressing what was actually happening. This is not how a neutral marketplace should operate. If a platform allows one member to extract data, bypass the system and gain a competitive advantage, it undermines trust for everyone using it. There is a good platform underneath, but governance, enforcement and data protection standards need serious improvement. Until that happens I would advise businesses to be cautious about what data they share and how they operate on here.

I don’t usually write reviews, as I like to give places the benefit of the doubt and I know how tough the hospitality industry can be.

I ordered a gluten-free “toastie”. Unfortunately, the word toastie is not the correct term, as it is labelled underneath in small writing as a gluten-free roll. A cold roll, may I add. This was really upsetting, as I completely missed where it said roll and was very excited about receiving a warm gluten-free toastie, which are hard to find when eating out.

My advice would be to change the word toastie to roll, as it is very misleading on your menu. After seeing the toastie pictures online, I was quite taken aback by the size of the gluten-free “toastie”. I understand you have priced these the same as the regular toastie, which is great to see. My dog was referred to Cave due to being diagnosed with Lymphoma. They were very quick to get in touch the next day and book my precious boy in we were so pleased. Went in for our consultation, we were advised it was stage 3/4 lymphoma and they took some bloods. Bloods came back and actually revealed it was stage 5. So that was the first unconfirmed and wrongly advised piece of information we were given. My dog was ok to go ahead with 1st dose of chemotherapy. A week later we went back and although he did have a tough time that week with side effects we went in and the oncologist told us in his words.... The cancer is dead, there is no more cancer in his bone marrow, he has probably lost weight due to the cancer cells being killed off. He then followed it up in the last sentence of, We will double check with our external lab who do more detailed analysis to confirm this. I get the results back, cancer has not been fully killed off but specialist is happy with the way things are going. A week later we go back, and he is some how riddled with cancer again. And this time a very different conversation was had. Totally floored us emotionally from one minute to be told he is cancer free, oncologist was smiling from ear to ear, and now this week complete opposite. You CANNOT so easily give this false hope to people who live their lives with their pets as part of the family, who would do anything for them, without first getting the facts correct and just guessing. One minute we are being told our vets blood machines don't work properly and theirs are much better. But isn't it strange how all of a sudden when my dog was no longer - quote 'Cancer free' that we were then told their machines are also not reliable!!!. We were advised it was ok to go ahead with third dose of chemo but this time it would be the decider as to whether they would continue if this had little change to the cancer or he was unable to tolerate it well. You can imagine the absolute shock given what we were told 7 days earlier. Given this was our last chance to help our little boy we went ahead. We were very concerned he had a temperature and had no immune system and pushed for antibiotics but were told no. We left, and under two days later my world came crumbling when he suddenly passed away. Not once were we warned that this was ever on the cards. We were given false hope twice and denied the full facts. We trusted this specialist with my whole world. Then to top it off, the lab my vets used to test the blood reported it was an extremely rare form of Plasmaoblastic Lymphoma - with only a few reported cases in the world. Our specialist rejected claims it was this as it was unheard of and requested more tests. Just as Wilson passed away further histology came back and confirmed it was indeed this rare lymphoma.
I give the 1 star for the absolutely lovely team on reception, and would advise that for all pet owners sake vets provide realistic factual advise to pet owners before giving false hope.

one_star_reviews.text:
Generally I prefer to stick to the positive reviews, but I think it’s only fair to share my experience. I’ve kept this to Google to ensure it sits within a broader range of feedback, as I’m conscious of not unfairly influencing platforms with only a small number of reviews. My intention is to offer transparency not to damage reputation.

I was initially encouraged by the company’s claim of having “decades of property sales experience,” as local knowledge and professionalism were important factors for me but ultimately, I experienced what can only be described as a “heritage” approach to estate agency. A true throwback that I can only assume peaked somewhere between the late 90s and early 2000s… judging by the reliance on handwritten scraps of paper to record important details. A bold choice in 2026.

The valuation process was, well… enlightening. Despite claiming strong local knowledge, I was quoted initially £350k for a property in Council Tax Band E, in an area where comparable homes are sitting between £420k and £600k (with recent sales around £525k). My face obviously did the talking as when I queried this it was raised to £375k with a need to review it after 4 weeks. I didn’t however feel there was a particularly clear or confident rationale behind the figure, just a vague sense that this was “about right.” Reassuring.

Needless to say, I didn’t come away with a clear sense of how my property would be actively positioned or sold. There appeared to be an assumption it would largely sell itself, to be fair at that price point it probably would, however in all seriousness, there was no real indication of proactive buyer engagement or use of local knowledge around schools, transport links, or amenities.

I’m glad I opted not to sign on the dotted line as it were, or who knows multi-part carbon paper.

For context, I have since received an offer of £425k from another agent prior to going to market, which does raise questions about the original valuation.

On a positive note, the fees are competitive, however, my experience suggests there may be a reason for that.
All in all, a fascinating opportunity to experience both ends of the estate agent spectrum. I just hadn’t expected to get the “worst” quite so vividly.

My mother-in-law died yesterday at St Peter’s Hospital, and I want to share our experience of her time on a geriatric ward.

Overall, we found the experience upsetting and, at times, lacking in clear communication and coordination. It also felt, to us, that compassion was not always as evident as it could have been. Kindness is cheap and effective.

We encountered basic administrative errors that were unsettling. For example, while the medical team did manage to obtain a DNR order, her name was at one point recorded incorrectly, and her next of kin was initially listed as her late husband.

In our experience, communication with the medical team was inconsistent. Important discussions about her condition and prognosis sometimes took place without family involvement because she was deemed to have capacity.

While we understand the legal basis for this, we found it difficult and distressing that these conversations happened without any relatives present, given her frailty and that they concerned the end of a loved one’s life.

We often felt we had to actively seek updates rather than being kept informed. On one visit, we were distressed to find that food, fluids, and some treatments had been withdrawn, which we had not fully understood in advance.

We also felt that she did not always receive timely help with basic needs like eating, drinking, or going to the toilet unless family members were there to assist or prompt staff. We recognise that staff are under pressure, but this was hard to witness.

We found conversations around end-of-life decisions, including resuscitation status and withdrawal of treatment, food and water, difficult to navigate. From our perspective, these discussions were not initially handled with the clarity or sensitivity we would have hoped for, although one longer meeting later on was more helpful.

There were also moments of visible tension between relatives of other patients and members of the medical team, which contributed to an already stressful environment.

At one stage, we were told that the ward manager was working from home, which we found surprising and added to a sense of disconnection.

I would encourage other families to stay closely involved, be present as much as possible, ask questions, and double-check important details if a loved one is admitted to a St Peter’s geriatric ward.

Despite previously leaving a 5-star review two years ago and having a positive initial experience, I unfortunately now feel compelled to update this to a 1-star review following two unacceptable tenancy exit experiences.

As a landlord based in Australia, I rely entirely on Meyers’ full property management service, for which I pay approximately 10% of the monthly rent. This makes it even more disappointing that I have felt unsupported and poorly represented throughout.

During my first tenancy changeover, several issues arose:

- I was required to pay half of the cleaning costs due to an inadequate report, despite the tenants vacating the property (email evidence attached).
- There was a complete lack of communication regarding white goods being paid for by incoming tenants. Meyers contacted another party directly without informing me and attempted to allow previous tenants access to remove a large fridge freezer and washing machine after their bond had already been returned, leaving me exposed to potential damage with no funds held to cover any issues.
- Communication was at times unprofessional, including inappropriate remarks such as “blimey”.
- The exit report itself was concerning. It rated the property as “good” despite clear issues, including visible damage, paint on plug sockets, damage to the bath panel, an unreported leak from the bathroom above, an unclean oven with oil and food residue, and a stained sink (photographic evidence attached).

one_star_reviews.text:
I was extremely disappointed with my recent experience regarding the referral process at St Giles Vets.

My dog had already been assessed by the out-of-hours service in what was a time-sensitive and urgent IVDD case, where prompt referral and specialist input are widely recognised as critical to outcomes. Despite this, I was still required to follow the practice’s internal referral process before a referral could be made. This caused unnecessary delay, additional stress, and additional expense at a point when urgent action was needed.

I also found my interaction with the vet to be abrupt and inflexible, and I did not feel that my interests or my pet’s welfare were treated with sufficient importance given the urgency of the situation. There appeared to be little recognition of the clinical seriousness of the case or the fact that my dog had already been assessed out of hours. The insistence on following the standard process risked further deterioration in my dog’s condition and delayed access to appropriate urgent care.

This ultimately resulted in me being charged £365 for the referral, as St Giles advised it was being made at my request rather than based on the clinical information already available and guidance from Cave Veterinary Specialists. This cost was avoidable and arose because the practice required an additional in-person assessment despite my dog already being seen out of hours.

When I raised these concerns with the centre manager, I was initially told the process would be reviewed. However, after I was required to present detailed supporting evidence, it was ultimately decided that no change was needed. This left me feeling that neither my interests nor my pet’s welfare were prioritised. In a situation where no one needed to lose, I was left financially disadvantaged.

As someone who advocates for cat cafes, rescue and the wellbeing of cats I was excited to go here.

This place absolutely missed the mark. We booked in advance and were greeted by 4 staff members sat at the door, three didn’t say a word just stared at us slumped and one gave us an intro and some rules to read. The unfriendly cats are pointed out to you on arrival also. There is a door that leads in to the cafe and there seems little urgency in ensuring this is shut so that the cats cannot escape.

We were showed to our table, there was one other group upstairs in the cafe, we had 4 staff members who sat around a table near us doing absolutely nothing. Fair enough if there’s nothing to be done but the cafe was absolutely filthy. There was so much dirt everywhere, piles of cat hair in the corners and on the trees that had clearly been there for weeks, not days. The glass is filthy, as are tables and toys. We were so uncomfortable that we chose not to order anything, so I cannot comment on the food.

The cafe was eerily quiet, no gentle music anywhere. The cats all gravitated downstairs so that’s where we went (cats do what they want so we had no expectation) downstairs smelt like litter and had even less ambience. Everything was so run down, cat trees were falling apart and everything was tatty. There were baskets of dirty cat toys. The cats seemed uninterested in humans, we all know cats sleep most of the day but I didn’t see one positive interaction. The cats coats were not particularly shiny as you would expect, I thought maybe they were newly rescued but have been there a while.

None of the staff spoke to us, just sat around gossiping and one came out of the kitchen in a flap and made this quite apparent to everyone else in the cafe.

I have been to some amazing cat cafes and I love to see a good cause. I’m not sure who this is benefiting as the cats did not seemingly want to interact and neither did the staff. A couple of the cats were described as scratchy or bitey, surely this suggests their time at a cafe may have expired or not be appropriate if they frequently react this way to interaction. Whilst there I read that the cafe was heavily funded by the community which seems a shame that it has been allowed to continue in the state that it’s in. The runs up high and the obstacles/shelves are amazing and maybe once this placed oozed with passion and love. Overall I felt so disappointed that I had spent my money on this, I have paid triple this to support a cat cafe and am happy to do so but I cannot get on board with pause. I’ve had a pretty frustrating experience with Cuckoo Fibre overall, despite some positives.

To start with the good: when the connection actually works, the speeds are genuinely very good. Streaming, downloads, and general browsing are all fast and stable at times, which is what you’d hope for from a fibre provider.

However, the issues around everything else have really let it down.

Customer service has been a major pain point. It often feels like the support team doesn’t fully understand what’s being asked, even for relatively simple requests. On multiple occasions, I’ve tried to get straightforward changes made and it’s either taken far too long or hasn’t been done correctly at all.

A big limitation is the lack of control over the router. You can’t make basic network changes yourself — things like opening ports, changing the WiFi password, or even renaming your network. This is incredibly restrictive, especially if you have smart home devices, gaming setups, or anything that requires port forwarding or custom configuration. Most providers allow at least some level of user control, so this feels unnecessarily locked down.

I’ve also had ongoing issues with devices struggling to connect reliably. There have been multiple engineer visits, and while they’ve confirmed there is a problem, no one seems able to identify the root cause. To make matters worse, the engineers aren’t directly employed by Cuckoo, so there’s a bit of a disconnect in accountability and follow-up.

On the administrative side, things haven’t been much better. I submitted a subject access request over 2.5 months ago and am still waiting for a response, which is well beyond expected timeframes. Formal complaints also seem to disappear into a void — I’m told responses have been sent, but I’ve never actually received them.

In summary, while the raw internet speeds are strong, the lack of router control, poor customer support, unresolved technical issues, and slow (or nonexistent) responses to formal requests make this a difficult service to recommend.

I feel completely robbed after using Patterson Law. If you are facing a license revocation, take my advice: save your thousands of pounds and just redo your theory and practical tests from scratch. It is much faster, cheaper, and less stressful than dealing with this firm's "service."

I paid a staggering £2,760 in legal fees, only to receive representation that was nothing short of embarrassing. Here is what you can expect for your money:

Zero Preparation: My assigned, rather elderly solicitor, Thomas Restell, arrived at my hearing on March 20, 2026, completely unprepared. He actually forgot to bring the supporting letter from my father, which was a vital piece of evidence for my defense.

Incompetent Advocacy: He barely defended me. He focused entirely on a "Wickens defense" and failed to mention any of the real-world implications of me losing my license. He didn't tell the judge how a disqualification would destroy my work life, my finance, or my mental health.

Poor Communication: They didn't even bother to tell me my father needed to be in court. I brought my mother instead, and when we realized the mistake, I had to rush my father to the court in a last-minute Uber. It was a total shambles.

Complete Loss: After all that money, I   still lost my license and was hit with £628 in court fines.

The Alternative: Once my license was revoked, I realized I’d been scammed by the legal process. I decided to put my mind to it and re do my theory test and after I passed I got lucky with a cancellation for a practical test, and managed to get my license back in around 6 weeks by redoing everything myself. It is entirely possible to do this if you try hard and have a bit of luck.
Don't waste your time or your hard-earned money on Patterson Law. You’re paying for a "premium" service and getting a defense that misses half the facts. Avoid them at all costs.

I placed an order which was meant to be delivered via Evri. The courier marked the parcel as delivered to a “safe place,” however the proof of delivery image was completely black and the item was not at the property or anywhere I could locate.

However, I was repeatedly told the claim could not proceed unless the form was fully completed in its original format. I was unable to do this despite trying multiple methods and explaining my accessibility limitations.

Unfortunately, the claim was eventually closed because I could not complete the form, even though all required information had already been provided in writing. Due to this I have not received my lost order.

Overall, I found the process very difficult and not accessible in my situation. I would not recommend this company.

We have a fleet of Renault Kangoos.
I have been informed that our vehicles may have a coolant recall.
I decide to call my local Renault Dealership - Platinum Yeovil to find out and book in for the work to be done.. simple enough right?

I have phoned about 6 times and I am no closer to knowing anything before I phoned up!
First call - got transferred to service, put on hold then hung up on!
Second call - a lady took a message for someone in service to get back to me (4 hours later still no call back)
Third Call - no answer
Fourth Call - Damian answered and said he would transfer me to service dept... again put on hold and hung up on!
Fifth Call - no answer
Sixth Call - no answer

This is my first time in dealing with Platinum.. I am gobsmacked at how are you guys still in business!?!

Unfortunately, my overall experience has been very disappointing. I was initially drawn to the R5 for its looks and excellent drive, and the purchasing process itself was smooth and positive. Sadly, that’s where the good experience ended.
Handover day was a mess. As I drove into the dealership, I immediately noticed a dent in the off‑side quarter panel, and the near‑side of the car had a visible masking line with overspray across roughly three‑quarters of the side of the vehicle. To the dealer’s credit, both issues were resolved reasonably quickly, but it certainly wasn’t the new‑car experience we had hoped for.

Not long after, I noticed water ingress affecting the battery indicator on the bonnet—apparently a known issue within Renault, though not acknowledged as such by this dealership. I arranged for it to be inspected, but on the first visit I arrived too early, and on the second occasion no one was available to deal with it, so the issue has simply been left unresolved.

The final straw came when I arranged a service just four days before the car’s one‑year anniversary. I coordinated this by taking my wife to work early, organising the school run, rearranging meetings, and blocking out travel time—only to be told on the day that the dealership has a single technician in the workshop, who had called in sick, so not to bring the car in.

Overall, while the car itself is excellent, the aftersales service and organisation at this dealership have been extremely frustrating and unreliable, and will definitely be a significant consideration when we come to replace the car.

I don’t usually leave negative reviews, but I felt disappointed enough after this visit that I wanted to share my experience.

Otto is a coffee shop I’ve been wanting to try for a while, so I was really looking forward to visiting. Unfortunately, the experience didn’t live up to expectations. When my friend, a baby, and I arrived, we weren’t greeted, which wasn’t a big issue, so we chose a place to sit. I moved a stool to the side so I could sit on a proper chair for stability while looking after the baby. Shortly after, a staff member came over and began rearranging the chairs to make space where I had moved the stool, which was fine.

When we were ready to order, I asked for a recommendation for matcha, I was told there was no rose matcha available but blueberry and tiramisu were popular. I then went to pay using my friend’s phone (for her drink first) and ordered a tiramisu drink. The staff member took payment but didn’t ask if I wanted anything else, she took the payment walked anyway and took food upstairs meaning i  had to wait to order the second drink later when she came back downstairs.

The drinks themselves were lovely, so no complaints there. However, during our visit we realised the baby needed changing. As the toilets were upstairs and there were only a couple of other customers who weren’t near us, we decided to quickly change the baby on the bench. A staff member came over and told us there was a toilet upstairs, so I asked if there was a baby changing facility. She just muttered “oh” and walked away, which left us unsure what we were expected to do, as the toilets upstairs were very small and not suitable for changing a very young baby. (Did she expect us to change him on the toilet seat?)

Later, a gentleman came in and made a friendly comment about the baby, and the staff member seemed to react negatively to this, and her attitude came across as quite poor.

Overall, I felt disappointed by the lack of hospitality and the fact that the café didn’t seem very accommodating for customers with a baby. It’s a shame because I had been really looking forward to visiting.

Avoid this company entirely unless you want to be actively lied to, have unauthorised amounts attempted to be taken from your account multiple times a day without your knowledge or consent, have a company secretly investigate taking you to court while looking you in the eye and offering payment plans, have your personal data handled so recklessly that other peoples private information ends up mixed into your own records, and be deliberately targeted with aggressive collection tactics while they are fully aware you are at your most financially and mentally vulnerable.

This is also a company that is actively sitting in the background waiting for the right moment to add charges, default your account, and make your situation significantly worse. They are not there to help you. Please look into your rights before you go anywhere near this service, and if you are already with them, look into your rights now.

Three years. A three hundred pound loan. I cannot say it clearly enough, please learn from my mistake.

For anyone already caught up with them, you are legally entitled to request a copy of everything they hold about you, completely free and by law. Email them and ask for a Subject Access Request, go through every single entry and compare it against your own bank records and messages, and look hard at anything that does not add up. You may have far more options than they want you to believe, and you do not have to accept the way this company has treated you.

As for me personally, I am in the process of taking this to the Financial Ombudsman, the Information Commissioner, potentially the Financial Conduct Authority, and further if necessary. I started this process as someone who was simply frustrated about their own situation. What I have uncovered since has changed that completely. I now genuinely believe it is my responsibility to make sure other people are warned, and to make sure this company either receives the serious overhaul and retraining it desperately needs, or faces the consequences of the way it has been operating

We had been in discussions over a vehicle for the past four days, and I want to start by recognising that Howard, the salesman we were dealing with, was excellent throughout. His communication, knowledge, and professionalism were a key reason we chose to pursue a car through this dealership rather than going ahead with a more local option. He genuinely added value to the process and gave us confidence in making such a significant purchase.

Unfortunately, we ended up missing out on the vehicle, as it was reserved by another party. This was particularly frustrating as I had called earlier in the day and was advised that the car was still available, albeit with some interest. Based on that, we intended to place a deposit before the end of the day.

Circumstances meant I couldn’t make contact the previous day due to prior commitments, and today Howard was not working. However, I am confident that had he been available, we would have moved forward and secured the car without delay.

What was most disappointing was the handling of the situation when I called to raise concerns. At no point were we made aware of how imminent the sale was. Had it been clearly communicated that the vehicle was likely to be reserved imminently, we would have acted immediately rather than waiting to speak with Howard.

Instead, I spoke with a manager who was dismissive and unwilling to acknowledge our position. The conversation felt unnecessarily defensive, with repeated emphasis placed on it being our fault for not acting sooner. While I fully understand that vehicles are sold on a first-come, first-served basis, the lack of empathy, accountability, and basic customer service was disappointing, especially given the value of the purchase involved.

A simple acknowledgement or a more considerate approach would have gone a long way. Unfortunately, this interaction significantly undermined what had otherwise been a very positive experience.

A real shame, as the service up until that point had been excellent.

A week goes by and the car hasn’t been delivered, my money taken, the salesperson apparently no longer working at the dealership with no one bothering to rectify the situation. I am now considering legal action.

I visited this chiropractic clinic for lower back and left shoulder pain, I was advised to schedule x10 weekly sessions. The initial treatments were fine and seemed routine, but on the final session, the practitioner applied intense acupressure with his thumb to my left shoulder/neck area for about a minute. It was extremely painful, and I had to ask him to stop. Hours later, the area became very tender, and by the next day, I had swelling below my left ear along with severe pain.
I reported it to the clinic, and they suggested a cold compress, assuring me it would resolve. Unfortunately, nearly two years later, the swelling and tenderness persist, and I have developed constant high-pitched tinnitus that has not stopped. Extensive tests (GP visits, ENT specialist, hearing tests, ultrasound, MRI) all came back normal, but the symptoms have dramatically impacted my daily life, I have tried various treatments without relief..
While the staff was polite, this experience makes me question the practitioner's skills and understanding of safe techniques, especially for sensitive areas like the neck. I would not recommend this clinic if you are dealing with similar issues, please consider other options to avoid potential long-term harm.

Proceed with caution.

I’m not sure whether this review applies to Orbital10 Yeovil or Allen Computer Services, because both businesses seem to be registered at the same address, so I honestly don’t know which company we spoke to.

I visited the shop on Wednesday with a MacBook that had been spilled on with a very small amount of coffee with milk. The computer was still turning on and making the startup sound, but then immediately shutting itself off. You could only see the Apple logo for about two seconds.

At the shop, we were told that the computer was completely dead, all data was lost, and can't be recovered due to the SDD being soldered onto the motherboard. As I had very important data on my laptop I specifically asked: “So there’s absolutely NOTHING that can be done to recover the data?” The response was: “No, NOTHING can be done, but you can leave the laptop with us for diagnostics for £40.00 to see if we can get it running, but it will have to be formatted, so all data will be lost nonetheless.'

We left.

I started searching online and found MacBook-repairs. I shipped the laptop the very same Wednesday (for fast track diagnostic at a cost of £50.00) and by Friday the laptop was already back with me, fully repaired, with ALL data recovered and intact. The total cost was £290.00 including fast track diagnostic, getting rid of the liquid and replacement of the lid sensor and audio jack.

Do you genuinely realise how much trouble such inaccurate and careless diagnoses can cause people? I could have just believed you and deal with the big trouble of losing the data. Do you understand how important the data on someone’s drive may be? Does any of that matter to you at all?

If you simply don’t know how to repair something, wouldn’t it be better to say so and refer customers to someone who can help, instead of telling them their request cannot be sorted? What exactly is the purpose of giving customers completely false information like this?

I understand that I should have had a proper backup, and unfortunately in this case I only had a partial one, but with all due respect, I genuinely feel misled.

I’m not sure whether this review applies to Orbital10 Yeovil or Allen Computer Services, because both businesses seem to be registered at the same address, so I honestly don’t know which company we spoke to.

I visited the shop on Wednesday with a MacBook that had been spilled on with a very small amount of coffee with milk. The computer was still turning on and making the startup sound, but then immediately shutting itself off. You could only see the Apple logo for about two seconds.

At the shop, we were told that the computer was completely dead, all data was lost, and can't be recovered due to the SDD being soldered onto the motherboard. As I had very important data on my laptop I specifically asked: “So there’s absolutely NOTHING that can be done to recover the data?” The response was: “No, NOTHING can be done, but you can leave the laptop with us for diagnostics for £40.00 to see if we can get it running, but it will have to be formatted, so all data will be lost nonetheless.'

We left.

I started searching online and found MacBook-repairs. I shipped the laptop the very same Wednesday (for fast track diagnostic at a cost of £50.00) and by Friday the laptop was already back with me, fully repaired, with ALL data recovered and intact. The total cost was £290.00 including fast track diagnostic, getting rid of the liquid and replacement of the lid sensor and audio jack.

Do you genuinely realise how much trouble such inaccurate and careless diagnoses can cause people? I could have just believed you and deal with the big trouble of losing the data. Do you understand how important the data on someone’s drive may be? Does any of that matter to you at all?

If you simply don’t know how to repair something, wouldn’t it be better to say so and refer customers to someone who can help, instead of telling them their request cannot be sorted? What exactly is the purpose of giving customers completely false information like this?

I understand that I should have had a proper backup, and unfortunately in this case I only had a partial one, but with all due respect, I genuinely feel misled.

I DO NOT recommend this shop.

While at the same time I was investigating Homebox Ltd for incorrect billing as the ad been charging myself for gas supply when there was no gas supply being paid as Huddle and Tru Energy had hi jacked the gas supply. I was claiming over charges from Homebox Ltd to settle the payments to huddle when my guy said I’m still right, I then bypassed huddle and went straight to Tru energy, requested an erroneous transfer request, explained what happened and they responded that I don’t qualify for a erroneous transfer request, responded back straight away and put every thing in point form:

-accidental sign up

10 MONTHS stuck between Huddle and Homebox Ltd of the worst bundle energy companies around, 10 months of complete stress to educate them on misrepresentation, false claims, unlawful gain practices and basic understanding of Ofgem rules.

Homebox Ltd recently closed my acc after law enforcement complaints and has review the over charges and compensating £450 for over charges on the gas supply.

Huddle I would expect as a maximum the basic erroneous transfer error compensation under the ofgem guidelines and at most the average usage you so clearly stated in your most recent bill to the value of £700 as compensation for the length, stress and the out of my own pocket problem YOUR mistake has caused.

I am going to be required to cover a bill to Octopus Energy now for a gas supply for the past 10 months.

You need to act responsibly and accountable in your conduct and the damage it has caused.

STAY AWAY FROM HUDDLE!!! NOTHING BUT HELL, I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND TO MY WORST ENEMY

An account was created in my name and I was switched from my previous energy supplier onto a far more expensive tariff without my knowledge or consent. To this day, I still do not understand how this happened. When I realised what had happened, I contacted Huddle by phone and email to cancel and dispute the account, only to be told it was “too late” and that I would face cancellation fees despite never agreeing to the switch in the first place.

From there, the entire situation became a nightmare. I received constant automated emails, texts, and payment demands for charges I was disputing. Responses to my emails appeared to go unanswered, whilst automated bot email payment reminders continued almost daily for bills that were significantly more than my previous supplier.

I later discovered Huddle had sent enforcement officers to my rental property, charging me £60 per visit simply to post letters through a letterbox at a property I do not live at.

Things escalated even further when the property was switched onto a prepayment meter without my consent. The house is fully electric with no gas supply, and this left 7 tenants without electricity, heating, hot water, Wi-Fi, cooking facilities, and security systems. An emergency electrician had to be called out before discovering the issue was the meter we were unaware of had run out of credit.

At the time I was backpacking abroad with very limited connectivity, and despite my managing agent explaining the seriousness of the situation affecting multiple tenants, Huddle refused to speak with him because the disputed account was created in my name. In the end, the only way he could get the electricity restored was by pretending to be me on the phone!

To finally leave Huddle, I was told I had to clear all alleged debt on the account, including enforcement charges and cancellation fees. I reluctantly paid £1,094 just to escape the situation and in order to switch back to my previous supplier. I was also told that the £200 credit I had recently topped up onto the meter would be refunded, which never happened.

Months later, despite no longer being with Huddle, they charged me £364 from my bank account unexpectedly. I never knowingly authorised this payment and can only assume my card details had been stored from a previous over the phone meter top-up. I then found more automated bot erroneous emails in my spam folder claiming I had an outstanding £0 balance on my account, to which monthly scheduled payments of £364 will be made to recover the outstanding debt of £0 – made no sense!

Trying to contact customer service has been one of the most frustrating parts of this entire ordeal. Calls are placed on hold endlessly, staff are unable to explain anything properly, callbacks never happen, and I have even been hung up on multiple times. I ended up having to cancel my bank card to avoid these unauthorised Huddle charges from continuing.

Now, despite previously settling the account and it being half a year since leaving Huddle for another energy provider, I am once again receiving threatening legal emails about alleged debts exceeding £1,100, with threats of CCJs and no proper explanation of the charges.

The amount of stress, inconvenience, wasted time, and financial loss this has caused has been unbelievable. I have now lodged a formal complaint and intend to escalate this matter further with Ofgem and any other relevant bodies if necessary.

I would strongly advise others to stay well clear of Huddle, and those of you who have left 1 star reviews to escalate the matter further. Companies running like this should not exist.

one_star_reviews.text: They charge 15 pounds for THREE croquettes! Ridiculous price! Maybe consider writing how many you serve on the menu? Because that’s a scam.

My goodness! I really cannot remember the last time I had such a horrible dining experience. Sexy Lobster has opened with a marketing bang, accompanied by a web site that might as well be AI-generated, since the reality is far removed from the cleverly "tweaked" photographs. The interiors are tired, dated, awkward, and nothing has changed since it was NEO.

In fact, the whole identity of the restaurant seems confused, with the menus referencing both NEO and Sexy Lobster. There is no semblance of a staff uniform, which adds to the lack of cohesion. Service was perfunctory, and one waiter verged on plain rude.

The à la carte menu is small, which is fine as long as it is inspiring; Sexy Lobster's is not inspiring in any way. The presentation of the food was so bad, it was almost as if a child had plated it. Never before have I had a tuna steak served to me pre-cut! Why would you do this? It meant the fish was cold by the time it reached the table. It was also served in a puddle of purée. The chocolate mousse with hazelnut crumb and ice cream was literally dollops in a bowl. I had stopped taking photos at this stage, as everything was just so poor.

Diners on the table next to us asked for condiments. These were served to them in those little glass jars that pubs and chain restaurants use. A decent restaurant would at least decant these and serve in small dishes. Watching a waitress trying to keep a candle alight on a small birthday offering for one of the tables was straight out of Fawlty Towers.

The apparent pedigree of Sexy Lobster is diametrically opposed to the reality. If I were the Executive Chef, I'd be removing my name from the web site. The site shows beautifully presented dishes; the reality was the most embarrasing-looking dishes I have ever seen in all my many years of dining.

Two main courses, one side, two desserts, a bottle of wine, a glass of wine, a bottle of water, and service charge came to a jawdropping £168.14! I have paid considerably less at good restaurants in London. I will add at this point that we got a promotional 20% discount - which we had to ask for, even though it was included in the booking details - but £134.51 was still an outrageous price (and still more than many London restaurants).

No doubt people will go to Sexy Lobster for the location and because of the slick marketing, but I can't see much repeat business at these prices and for the standard of the food and the whole experience. I will not be returning to another Dorset dining disappointment that is Sexy Lobster.

I have been playing at GZ for just over ten years, supported the GZ and ZO brand, attended a few NAEs and it's frustrating to see how much this site has declined. I have been reasonably polite about the quality of the site, however I feel as if I can no longer bottle my experiences up and action must happen now.

Please note that this review is mostly about the Sunday games which seems to attract the most players.

Within the past three years, I have witnessed both marshal and player behaviours sour to unacceptable levels. Many are standoffish, disengaged and unwilling to manage player conduct. I have witnessed marshals verbally abusing players and even arguing with each other which sets a terrible tone and undermines any sense of professionalism.

This lack of leadership feeds directly into the major gameplay issues. Player conduct can be poor, rules are inconsistently enforced and the general attitude across the site has noticeably deteriorated into dangerous levels. It's no surprise to me that frustrated players often leave during the lunch hours which makes balancing and gameplay quality worse as the day progresses.

Game organisation is another serious issue I've noticed. Sundays play as one long continuous objective without any breaks, sort of like a milsim, but without the structure, planning or discipline that makes these sort of games work. By the afternoon the lack of resets or scenario changes leads to severe team balancing problems and a big drop in player retention leaving the remaining teams a lopsided low-energy experience.

The site itself still has potential but the unmanaged woodland of primarily rhododendron bushes make navigating large areas frustrating rather than tactical. They block routes, create pointless choke points and slow down movement in ways that don't add any value to gameplay.

On top of all this, the increase in price from a few years ago makes the value even harder to justify. To quote another player's perspective, it would seem that management are more focused on revenue rather than utilising these funds to enhance the gameplay or player experience. Taking these views, to me it feels as if the quality has sharply fallen while the price has gone up. I understand that cost of living pressures without a doubt influenced this increase, but the issue remains that the quality has dropped significantly.

Despite the problems with the site, there are genuine positives worth acknowledging.

There are staff who are friendly and there's a good number of positive enthusiastic regular players who try to help keep the atmosphere enjoyable. There are a good handful of marshals who genuinely do try their best. They're engaged, helpful and clearly care about the people but unfortunately their efforts are often overshadowed by colleagues with far poorer attitudes.

A standout feature is the Second Hand table ran by Rich. He's an absolute top bloke, honest, friendly and helpful, always looking to give a fair price and solid advice. For many players including myself, he is what stands out the most for the GZ experience. I genuinely cannot recommend him enough.

After a decade of playing here it is clear that the site needs new management, proper restructuring and better run games if it wants to return to the level it once had. There is a solid core of good people at GZ, both staff and players.

Ground Zero can be great again but not without serious changes. At this stage I cannot recommend GZ. A Sunday game here is NOT an appropriate introduction to airsoft if you're interested in the hobby.

one_star_reviews.text:
Been going here for a while and always use the 40% offer as that makes it justifiably affordable (me, wife and three children) to eat out, however I won't be going back after today.
We didn't book as it was a last minute choice, never had an issue doing this in the past. We walked in the door and into the seating area we've always sat in however every table was reserved, no problem, its a big enough place. We were then shouted at by someone asking if we were alright. I said we'd like to eat is there anywhere to sit and he says "No. Have you booked" in a really sarcastic voice and just stood staring at us, hands pressed together. I then had to fill the gap and ask if there was space somewhere else to which in a huffy voice he replies well I may be able to squeeze a high chair on the end of a table... The only thing missing from his zero patience reply was an eye roll. He then walked off and we assumed we should follow him. At this point I'm already pissed off, we chose this business to enter and spend our money and this guy who we don't know is being disrespectful in the way he's talking, not only to me but also to my wife.

We sat down and chose our food on the app before we chose our drinks, however the 40% code wouldn't work so my wife went to order at the bar. When she mentioned that the code wasn't working the same guy smirked and says "uh yeah it's bank holiday weekend? It's not going to work?" Proper attitude and that was enough for us, when my wife told me about the way he spoke to her again, i said lets go.

Obviously the drop in price is part of the reason we go here, eating out in this financial climate is a treat when you're feeding 5 people, our food alone would've been over £70 and we would've easily spent another £30 on drinks plus possibly puddings. There's absolutely no way I'm putting over a hundred quid through the till of a business being 'managed' by an absolute self obsessed, stuck up idiot who's pissed off because he's working on a bank holiday weekend. He is so overly confident in the way he delivers his blunt and unnecessary responses, if it wasn't so disrespectful I'd laugh.

This guy either wanted people to know he was way above being there, or was genuinely wanting someone to either leave, or ask him if he was alright. Either way, not someone who should be front of house, greeting people or having to do any task that requires doing anything as he's either not being paid enough in his mind to do it, or he genuinely just thinks he's above people who come in and choose to spend the equivalent of half a weekly food shop in one sitting with that business. He's a let down not only the business, but the rest of the team there as we've always had a really nice experience every time we've eaten or drank here.

I work hard for the money I earn, as does everyone, and moraly I'm never handing it over to anyone who treats others like that. The sad part is going by his character, he's the type to read this and think he's winning and that these observations are 'just bang on to his aura, just who he is'.

In the end we went next door and grabbed a McDonald's! Wincanton branch has been rated one of the best in the country and although the staff are worked to the bone, always have a smile on their face, always cheery and professional. I'll be popping an email to Marstons with my experience and my advice for anyone still reading this debating whether to pop in and try this place, check reviews on other places first and go elsewhere. Reading other reviews on the Wagtail, attitudes seem to be an issue although as mentioned, we've always been made to feel welcome up until todays experience with this 'main character' member of staff.

Proper disappointing and no doubt Marstons have lost a considerable amount of money overall through potential customers meeting this insufferable character. Overall, disappointing waste of time and his presence just caused the atmosphere to seem dead. Find a job that doesn't involve people.

I went all the way here (from east Christchurch) because it was supposed to be 'Poole and Bournemouth Exhaust Repair Centre', with there website saying "most exhausts don't need replacing, the can be repaired". We stopped at this pub on our way home from a weekend away, having gone out of our way after looking at reviews, and honestly, I wish we hadn’t bothered. If I could give zero, I would.

The food was hugely disappointing; all of the vegetables were pale, unappetising and rock hard! The beef, which we were told would be pink, was very pink to the point of being off-putting. We ate the beef purely so it wouldn’t go to waste, but we left the vegetables and potatoes untouched. As well as the extra potatoes we ordered.

To be clear, the issue was not with the floor staff they were polite and friendly young girls who were busy the whole time we were there. The problems were entirely down to how things were handled at the bar by what I assume would be the manageress.

When we raised that we weren’t happy, the manageress’s first response wasn’t to ask what was wrong with the food, but to ask whether anyone had checked on our table; which they hadn’t. Hence we’d approached the bar to settle the bill ourselves.
It immediately felt like she was trying to shift blame onto her staff rather than actually listen to the issue.  Which was at all fair!

When I did begin explaining the problems with the meal, she abruptly asked “what was wrong with it then” and then walked off mid-conversation, clearly uninterested… to make drinks for other customers.

Her attitude throughout was incredibly rude; she was argumentative from the get go. Like we were making up that there were issues with the clearly untouched two, near full, plates of food/ sides. She marched over to our table shaking her head, inspected our plates in a dismissive way, and took them straight to the kitchen herself. The whole interaction felt hostile and unnecessary.

Despite everything, the manageress tried to charge us for the full meals. I calmly explained that I was more than happy to pay for the beef we had eaten, but not for the sides we hadn’t touched. She responded by saying she “wasn’t going to argue” despite the fact I hadn’t been argumentative at any point. She entered the interaction with attitude

She then claimed she had already removed one of the beefs but still insisted on charging for the rest, including the untouched potatoes. When I asked for those to be taken off, she caused a scene, again with a rude tone, and demanded to know what I did want to pay for…. Like I was being unreasonable for asking for untouched food to be taken off..Which I had explained a couple of times… a whole other argument over £3 of a side of a potatoes.

Overall, while the floor staff themselves were friendly, the poor food and the manageress’s dismissive, confrontational and outright rude behaviour completely ruined the experience. Definitely not somewhere I’d return to or recommend!!

I’ve run pubs/ bars myself for long enough to understand everyone has off days; as do businesses. But there was not that. The treatment received today was wholly unnecessary and totally unacceptable!

I purchased an EV from Penton in November 2023. While I absolutely loved the car itself, my experience with the dealership has been appalling. I was completely misinformed and mis-sold about the real-world range; specifically, I was never told how significantly motorway driving drains the battery compared to city driving. As a new EV owner, you rely on the "experts" to explain these nuances, but I was left to find out the hard way that the promised figures didn't translate to my actual usage.

Beyond the car itself, I was mis-sold a 3-year Penton service plan  (3 MOTs and 3 services, price £599 at the time). When I brought it in for its first service & MOT , I was told the car only needs a service every 2 years - meaning they sold me a plan I literally I did not need.

The aftercare is the worst I’ve experienced. I drove out of my first service with a tire sensor warning, only to be told I’d need to pay £200 for a diagnostic check. It turns out they simply hadn't inflated the tires correctly during the service. To be asked for £200 to fix their own oversight is daylight robbery.

I haven’t even tried to contact them directly about the service plan because whenever I’ve tried to challenge them in the past, like I did with the tires, I’ve been met with nothing but attitude.

My advice: The car was great, but do your own detailed research before buying. Don't rely on what the sales team tells you about range, and challenge every "additional cost" they try to slide past you. Avoid this garage if you value honesty and respect.

Based on this experience, I would recommend ensuring that any agreed refund terms are clearly documented and honoured.

one_star_reviews.text:
We recently visited Rick Stein Sandbanks having looked forward to the experience for quite some time. Unfortunately, the evening proved to be one of the most disappointing dining experiences we have had in a long time and fell far below the standards we would expect from a restaurant carrying such a strong reputation and premium pricing.

From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere felt cold and unwelcoming. The lady greeting us did not smile, did not appear pleased to see us, and gave the impression that our arrival was an inconvenience rather than a valued booking. When we explained it was our first visit, the response felt oddly surprised rather than welcoming.

Sadly, this lack of warmth and hospitality continued throughout the evening. Not a single member of staff made us feel genuinely welcome. There was little attentiveness, no effort to build rapport, and very little sense of customer care. Compared with other high-end restaurants we have visited, where service is polished, warm and proactive, the difference here was striking.

The starters arrived tepid. All three members of our party commented on this immediately after taking a bite. We politely raised the concern, expecting perhaps an apology or some understanding. Instead, we were repeatedly told that they “do not serve tepid food.” The way this was communicated felt dismissive and almost accusatory, as though our observations were somehow false or exaggerated. The interaction became uncomfortable and confrontational, despite us raising the concern politely.

What was most disappointing was not the issue itself, but the complete lack of empathy, professionalism and customer care shown in response to it.

We asked to speak to a manager, but this was not forthcoming. It was only towards the end of the meal, after reminding staff for a second time, that Leonard eventually attended the table. He arrived carrying a standard business card, did not introduce himself, did not apologise, and simply handed over the card without explanation. Only after being directly asked did he identify himself as Leonard and explain that he was a supervisor, writing his name onto the card in front of us. Again, the interaction lacked professionalism, accountability or genuine concern for customer experience.

Eventually the starters were replaced and removed from the bill, which we appreciated, although this was not something we had requested.

I had ordered the halloumi starter, which I found bland, and politely asked whether there were any alternative accompaniments available. Rather than attempting to accommodate the request, I was simply told that adding anything else would “ruin the dish.” No alternatives were offered and the response again felt dismissive and abrupt.

The mains arrived hot, which was an improvement, but the food overall was mediocre at best. Nothing we ate — lobster, steak, mussels or fishcakes — justified either the reputation of the restaurant or the prices being charged.

Service throughout the meal continued to disappoint. Our table repeatedly had to pour our own wine, and staff only returned occasionally to assist. One member of our party briefly left the table and returned several minutes later to find crumbs still present and the napkin untouched in exactly the same position. These are very basic service standards that most restaurants at this price point would manage without issue.

Perhaps most tellingly, when we left the restaurant, not a single member of staff apologised for the experience, thanked us for visiting, or even said goodbye.

Had the starters not been removed from the bill, the meal would have cost approximately £160 per person. For the quality of food, level of service and overall ambience we experienced, this felt significantly overpriced and overrated.

Ultimately, the best thing about this restaurant is the view. Sadly, based on our experience, we would not recommend the dining experience, customer service or atmosphere.

Avoid this shop at all costs!!!!!!
I want to share my full experience with this shop involving an iPhone 15 Plus battery replacement.

I originally had my back glass repaired at another shop. After that repair, my phone battery began overheating and expanding, which is when the issues started.

I then brought my phone to this shop. I was told the battery was at risk of exploding and needed immediate replacement, so I paid for a new battery.

For a short time afterwards the phone seemed fine, but it then developed serious ongoing issues including rapid battery drain (dropping around 30%), overheating, and microphone/volume faults where sound cuts in and out. The phone now has to stay on charge almost constantly to function properly.

I later had the device assessed by Apple, who confirmed ongoing battery issues as they had fitted an used/broken one into my phone. and advised further repairs are needed, including replacement work to access internal components due to suspected internal damage.

When I contacted the shop for a refund, I was told it was “suspicious” that I had not returned to the store sooner. I do not agree with this. The issues began after the repair, and I did initially raise concerns when the problems started, but I did not feel comfortable returning again afterwards.

I was also told that Apple were “trying to scam me,” which I strongly disagree with, as their assessment was based on a professional inspection of the device.

In response to my refund request, I was given a warranty statement, however no clear dates, duration, or start period were ever provided at the time of repair. This means there is no clear warranty timeline, and it has been used as a reason to refuse a refund.

Their warranty policy on their website:
Our warranty covers [specify the items or services covered] for a period of [mention the duration] from the date of purchase. During this time, we commit to repairing or replacing eligible products free of charge.

However, my complaint is not just about warranty — it is about the quality of the repair and the ongoing faults that followed it.

In total, I am now facing significantly higher repair costs due to what I believe was a faulty repair, and I have proof of all payments and repair history.

I am sharing this so others are aware of my
experience.

*** update, I did send over the bank statements, of the date and time of when I payed for the repair. So that is proof enough of a receipt, and as we discussed over text i was in under a year ago, so the 2024 comment is totally unnecessary to this review.

one_star_reviews.text:
We love visiting farm shops and always make an effort to support local businesses, especially those championing local produce and independent brands. Initially, our visit to Barleymows Farm Shop was genuinely lovely. The shop itself is beautifully stocked with many of the brands we enjoy supporting, and the deli counter had a fantastic selection of pastries, cheeses and cakes. The lady serving us there was warm, helpful and a real credit to the business.

As we continued shopping, we placed our items directly into our own reusable tote bag rather than taking a basket, something we regularly do to avoid unnecessary plastic bags and because we did not initially expect to buy very much. However, the selection was so good that we ended up filling the bag while deciding what meat to choose for a cassoulet we were making that evening.

At this point, a member of staff, who appeared to be some sort of manager, approached us holding a basket and asked if we would like one. We politely declined and explained that our bag was fine as we had nearly finished shopping anyway. Unfortunately, rather than simply leaving it there, we were met with the comment: “Well next time you visit, please use a basket instead of putting the items in your bag.”

The tone and implication behind the comment were incredibly uncomfortable and immediately changed the atmosphere of what had been a really pleasant visit. We were genuinely stunned and left feeling as though we were being indirectly accused of SHOPLIFTING! Had the interaction ended with the offer of a basket, we would have happily completed what was turning into quite a large shop and likely visited the café too. Instead, we felt so uncomfortable and offended that we decided to leave.

We approached the staff member to clarify what exactly she was implying. She insisted she was not implying anything and dismissively told us that she "liked" all of her customers to use baskets. However, there was no apology whatsoever for how the comment came across or the tone in which it was delivered. The interaction felt unnecessarily passive aggressive and patronising, as though we were being spoken to like children rather than paying customers.

What is particularly disappointing is that the rest of the team were genuinely lovely and helpful, which made this interaction stand out even more. Customer service is not just about what is said, but how it is said, and unfortunately this particular member of staff completely soured the experience for us.

It is a real shame because we had every intention of becoming regular customers. Instead, we left and took our custom elsewhere. Thankfully, we later visited Rumwell Farm Shop & Restaurant where we were made to feel welcome and appreciated as customers, regardless of how we happened to be carrying our shopping to the till.

one_star_reviews.text:
Good wine, good service, bad food.

I will start by mentioning the staff were lovely and the service and wine were top notch.

The food however wasn’t up to standard at all - very disappointing for something on the Michelin guide.

We came for the scollops which were very nice, but the sweatbread dish was not worth the money and came ill prepared with a sticker on - not right for a fine dining dish at that price point.

The mains left much to be desired, we had Brill which was watery and bland and the the Guinea foul had too many components on the plate, was over complicated and poorly presented. Whilst the ingredients were clearly very high quality, in general food lacked flavour, seasoning and uniqueness.

Despite lovely location and sweet staff we sadly are coming away feeling unsatisfied and still hungry.

We wanted to love it but to be honest the food is not the fine dining experience we expected and given price tag it’s a big shame

one_star_reviews.text:
Waited 40 minutes for an order of pancakes, not busy as only 3 tables of people but no one checked on us.  I ended up having to ask where the food was. The order had not been put through to the kitchen. There was no offer of discount for wasting our time, I cancelled the food and was still made to pay for 1 small drink. Not going back, don't recommend.
Group size
2 people
1+ hour

On the 19th of April 1:30pm ish me and my boyfriend came in to have some breakfast on the morning of our anniversary. We ordered an iced latte, an apple juice, a veggie 52 breakfast, and a full 52 breakfast with meat. We were told there would be a bit of a wait, and we accepted. The man said it would be 30 minutes, so we sat outside and expected our drinks to tie us over. We never ever got the drinks. He brought out the food after 50 minutes-1 hour. Maybe actually longer than that.

The mushrooms were raw, the egg was like a rubber disk and a raw egg yolk, the beans were cold, the sausage looked raw, and bacon looked congealed with fat and the “toast” wasn’t even toasted it was sliced bread. We kept asking about the drinks and never were given them. I’ve worked in cafes serving hot and iced drinks for over 3 years and an ice latte takes me under 5 minutes to make. A glass of apple juice is poured from a cartoon 🤦🏼‍♀️

When my partner took my food back to the guy behind the counter he immediately started making a new breakfast but I didn’t want it anymore so he was told not to replace it.

We saw another lady come and join him halfway through our long long wait for two drinks and two meals and it just baffles me with two people behind there they cannot even get us our drinks.

We went to the counter at the end together, and explained (politely) our food was not good, and we never got drinks. The lady stared confused and the man was confused. I said we never got our drinks and he still tried to charge us them, and we told him we didn’t get them and he removed one of the drinks, and we told him again, we got none of them. I said I am not paying for the meal I got as I didn’t even really touch it and it wasn’t good. My boyfriend said his food was also bad but he was made to pay for it. We also saw other customers who had been there after we arrived served first. An old man came in 20-30 minutes into our wait and was served immediately. Extremely rude behaviour favouriting other customers. I’ve worked in hospitality for almost a decade and I have always learnt first come, first served. This place is disorganised, confused, and rude. Also, the man apologised to my partner and not even me, he said “sorry sir” and not anything to me, i was very offended by that.

We used to visit quite often. More so in summer because of the outside seating. But the place has really gone downhill. It looks nice inside, beautiful decor, lovely seating area and I have always enjoyed the music they play in there as well. But that occasion the music was particularly loud, especially the speakers outside the front. I’m upset to say I will not return as it is my most local cafe, and I always found the food to be tasty but its turned out really badly. I think they were very understaffed that day, and I ultimately feel bad for the young chap behind the counter, but also he lacked major customer service skills. If he had addressed the situation better I wouldn’t have even written this as it’s clearly an understaffing problem. But he served others first, and tried to charge us for disgusting food and missing drinks!
I wish the business all the luck in improving as it was a good place to chill before.

Waited 50 minutes for an avocado toast. There were only 3 tables occupied. Most of tables were empty. Any proper chef / kitchen should be able to handle this. Disaster. Thankfully had plenty of time before my train otherwise this bunch would have caused me to miss it.
